## Three questions

A historian turning a text into data asks three questions of it, and each has one decision only the historian can make. A model can do everything around that decision.

| | The question | The model does | You decide |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Clean** | Is this what the page says? | Flags what reads oddly | Read the page and rule |
| **Structure** | What is a record here? | Proposes fields, fills them, keeps the quotes | What counts, and whether the record changed the meaning |
| **Ground** | Who is this? | Retrieves candidates with evidence | Supported, unresolved, or wrong |

That is the whole lesson. The hour illustrates it with one page.

## One page

Walter Agar's letter, *The Tropical Agriculturist*, 2 July 1883, p. 66 ([scan](https://archive.org/details/tropicalagricult18831884colo/page/n83/mode/1up)). Two hundred and thirty-four words from a planters' quarrel about one cinchona tree. It contains:

- a sentence the OCR got wrong in a way that reverses its meaning (**clean**);
- a relationship the journal's editor states loosely and Agar states carefully (**structure**);
- a person with a strong identity, Henry Trimen, Director of the Royal Botanic Gardens at Peradeniya, and a person with none in any authority file, Agar himself (**ground**).

You do not need to know anything about cinchona. The dispute is context for thirty seconds.

## The hour

| Minutes | | |
|---|---|---|
| 0–5 | [The page](steps/01-question.qmd) | Where Trimen comes from, and the letter |
| 5–20 | [Structure](steps/02-structure-extract.qmd) | The model proposes a table and extracts records. Then you: did a careful statement become a flat one? |
| 20–30 | [Ground](steps/03-candidates.qmd) | The model retrieves candidates. Then you: supported, unresolved, or wrong? |
| 30–45 | [Clean, together](steps/04-review.qmd) | The OCR against the page, and what the correction becomes |
| 45–55 | [Exercise](review/index.html) | Three decisions, in the room or on Zoom |
| 55–60 | [Your own data](steps/07-your-data.qmd) | Taking the three questions to another collection |

Every live stage has a saved checkpoint in `outputs/`.

## What you need

A browser. The [exercise](review/index.html) runs from saved results and needs no account or key. Remote participants have the same pages and the same exercise; the exercise page has a button that copies a one-line summary of your decisions for the Zoom chat.
